palette.name: colorset1
contrast_notes: Error text uses #333e48 on #ffccd5; #e8002a is a labeled accent and not the sole error cue.
Keyboard focus uses #9e1b32 rather than the palette's low-contrast #cfcfcf focus token.
Success uses neutral confirmation text and a checkmark, not an unselected green token.

authored_component_copy.heading: Support queue
authored_component_copy.subtitle: Review requests, stage a priority change, and keep the latest successful queue visible.
authored_component_copy.search_help: Search by ticket ID or subject. Choose a request to edit its priority.
authored_component_copy.priority_help: Choose the priority that should be saved for the selected request.
authored_component_copy.edit_help: Changes remain staged until you save. Cancel restores the last saved priority.

authored_component_copy.error_message: The queue could not be refreshed. Try again; the last successful queue is still shown.

authored_component_copy.fallback_heading: Text-only fallback and local test notes
authored_component_copy.fallback_copy: Support queue: 2 requests. Selected request: T-104, “I cannot access my account”, priority High, status Pending. Choose a request, select a priority, then save or cancel. Use Refresh queue to retry a local refresh.
authored_component_copy.browser_fixture_note: This is a self-contained browser fixture. It does not call an assistant, server, or host API; browser download behavior is not host acceptance evidence.

accessibility_copy.busy_region_behavior: The queue region exposes aria-busy while a local save or refresh simulation is pending.
accessibility_copy.selection_state: Each request button exposes aria-pressed for the current selection.
accessibility_copy.tooltip_behavior: The Export CSV tooltip is available on hover and keyboard focus through aria-describedby and role=tooltip.
accessibility_copy.focus_behavior: All controls have a visible #9e1b32 focus ring and the invalid priority control receives focus.
accessibility_copy.status_cues: Feedback combines text with a symbol, and error styling adds a labeled accent; color is never the only cue.

H1.label: Visible status
H1.interaction: Opening, saving, refreshing, and failure feedback
H1.fix: Run the browser fixture and inspect each live-region transition.

H2.label: Familiar concepts
H2.interaction: Queue, request, priority, and status vocabulary
H2.fix: Keep protocol codes behind diagnostics and display labels beside controls.

H3.label: Control and exits
H3.interaction: Cancel edit and retry after refresh failure
H3.fix: Keyboard-test cancellation and confirm the draft is restored.

H4.label: Consistent conventions
H4.interaction: Button labels, staged edit, and keyboard-focus behavior
H4.fix: Compare native and terminal fallback labels when adapted to a host.

H5.label: Prevent mistakes
H5.fix: Choose the blank priority and verify the control receives focus without changing data.

H6.label: Recognition cues
H6.interaction: Labels, selected request, priority, status, and help
H6.fix: Inspect accessible names in a browser accessibility tree.

H7.label: Efficient paths
H7.interaction: Search, direct selection, clear search, and export
H7.fix: Exercise keyboard-only search and selection without pointer input.

H8.label: Minimal content
H8.interaction: Primary queue task with fallback in a disclosure
H8.fix: Check narrow layout and avoid introducing nested scrolling.

H9.label: Useful errors
H9.interaction: Refresh failure preserves the last successful queue
H9.fix: Trigger failure, verify recovery copy, then retry successfully.

H10.label: Contextual help
H10.interaction: Search, priority, export tooltip, and fallback help
H10.fix: Verify tooltip is reachable by keyboard and does not obscure recovery actions.
